translations.translatedText: # Saturday 2.6.2018 (radio)
It has been a celebration day in schools. The Naantali museum shows old professions. The new Archbishop of the Finnish church starts work. The weather will get colder at the start of next week.
## A student celebration
![A matriculation cap in the middle of roses.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-7998929)
Open image viewer
A matriculation cap and roses bring the celebration. Photo: Raila Paavola / Yle
It has been a celebration day in schools. The schools have finished and the summer holiday has started.
Almost 60,000 young people received their comprehensive school leaving certificate.
Around 27,000 young people celebrated their matriculation on Saturday. The new matriculated students have received matriculation caps and roses.
The time of matriculation celebrations is important for flower shops. Many flower shops are selling 10 times as many flowers this weekend as they would on an ordinary weekend.
This is also a time of celebration for all the students who have completed a vocational qualification. There are about 76,000 of them.
## Old professions

![The director of the Naantali museum, Anne Sjöström, and curator Mari Termonen try out the work of a switchboard operator.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-10208458)
Open image viewer
The director of the Naantali museum, Anne Sjöström, and curator Mari Termonen try out the tools of a telephone switchboard operator. Photo: Jouni Koutonen / Yle
Professions change with the times. This year the most graduates were practical nurses and business college graduates.
In the future some professions will disappear and some completely new ones will arise, as robots improve.

Many professions ended long ago. This summer the Naantali museum is showing professions that no longer exist. The museum has, for example, the tools of a comb maker, a fire lookout and a telephone switchboard operator.
The public can get to know old professions at the Naantali museum all summer long. Naantali is near Turku.
## A new Archbishop
![Archbishop Tapio Luoma](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-10233043)
Open image viewer
The new Archbishop Tapio Luoma. Photo: Tanja Heino / Yle
The new Archbishop of the Evangelical Lutheran Church of Finland starts work. The new Archbishop is Tapio Luoma. Luoma was chosen as Archbishop in March.

At a service in Turku Cathedral on Sunday, Luoma will be installed in the office of Archbishop. A group of bishops from Finland and abroad are taking part in the service. Bishops from the Nordic countries, Estonia and Ireland are taking part. President Sauli Niinistö is also attending the service.
The Archbishop leads the Finnish church. In addition to the Archbishop, the Finnish church has 9 bishops. Each bishop has an area that they lead. Until now Tapio Luoma has been the Bishop of Espoo.
The new Archbishop Tapio Luoma is 56 years old. Luoma is a Doctor of Theology, and he has long worked as a priest and bishop. Luoma is married and has 3 adult children.
## The weather gets colder
![Canoeists at the Aurinkolahti beach in Helsinki on 29 May 2018.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-10235535)
Open image viewer
The weekend is still warm, then it gets colder. Photo: Onni Ojala / Lehtikuva
School end-of-term celebrations have been held in warm and sunny weather. Sunday is also still a beautiful day.

At the start of next week the weather will change. It will get colder. At the start of the week the weather will be clearly colder than now. In the north it may also rain. In the south it will be dry, which means no rain will fall.
